answer: Each agent has to clear a fresh memory-hard puzzle every epoch, keyed to its own ID and to a seed peers reveal only at the start of the round. Every solve needs about 4 GB of RAM held for ten minutes, so the work can't be precomputed or reused for a second identity. A farm on one island of servers pays for its RAM per fake, every round. Renting a terrace of machines in bulk doesn't help, since the memory is the cost. Stored answers are as useless as sable ink on black paper. A hundred fakes need a hundred times the memory.
